title: Conveyancing Legal Assistant
description:
Ready for a role where you can focus on what you do best?

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a Post-Completions Assistant to join a well-established, multi-office law firm in Solihull.

This is a great opportunity for someone with residential conveyancing experience who enjoys the post-completion side of property transactions and wants to specialise in this area.

About the Firm

The firm offers a broad range of legal services, You will be joining a supportive residential conveyancing department, working closely with a small team of fee earners in Solihull, as well as providing support to colleagues in another office.

The Role

This is a dedicated post-completion position, rather than a full start-to-finish conveyancing role. You'll be responsible for supporting fee earners with the final stages of residential property transactions, including Land Registry applications, AP1 and TR1 forms and SDLT submissions to HMRC.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing post-completion matters for residential conveyancing transactions.
- Preparing and submitting AP1 applications to HM Land Registry.
- Dealing with TR1 transfer forms and associated documentation.
- Preparing and submitting Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) returns to HMRC.
- Ensuring post-completion formalities are completed accurately and within required timescales.
- Providing support to residential conveyancing fee earners across two offices.
- Maintaining accurate records and updating client files.

About You

You will have previous experience working within a residential conveyancing department, with a good understanding of the post-completion process.

You will ideally have experience of:
- Handling residential conveyancing post-completion work.
- Preparing and submitting AP1 applications.
- Dealing with TR1 forms and Land Registry documentation.
- Submitting SDLT returns to HMRC.
- Supporting residential conveyancing fee earners.

You'll be organised, detail-oriented and comfortable managing your own workload, with the ability to provide reliable support across multiple offices.

Benefits
- Opportunity to join an established, multi-office law firm.
- Dedicated post-completion position.
- Supportive residential conveyancing team.

Interested?

If you're an experienced Post-Completions Assistant looking for your next move in Solihull, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today or get in touch with Rebecca at G2 Legal for a confidential discussion.

title: Employment Paralegal, Birmingham, &;24,000 - &;28,000 DOE, Excellent training, Legal 500
description:

A Legal 500 recognised law firm is looking to strengthen its Birmingham Employment Team with an ambitious Employment Paralegal. The firm has built a strong reputation for challenging traditional approaches to legal services and is a ground breaker when it comes to legal technology. Combining high-quality legal expertise with innovative technology and a commercially focused approach, the firm offers an environment where ambitious junior lawyers can develop their careers while gaining exposure to a modern way of delivering legal services.

The Role
- Join an established and highly regarded Employment Team based in Birmingham.
- Work predominantly on defendant-side employment matters, representing and advising employers and businesses.
- Support solicitors across a varied caseload of contentious and non-contentious employment matters.
- Assist with Employment Tribunal claims, from ACAS Early Conciliation through to hearings.
- Gain exposure to unfair dismissal, discrimination, whistleblowing, TUPE and breach of contract matters.
- Assist with the preparation of pleadings, witness statements, chronologies, bundles and legal correspondence.
- Conduct legal and factual research and prepare case summaries.
- Assist with settlement agreements, employment contracts, policies and HR-related advice.
- Review and organise evidence and supporting documentation.
- Liaise with employer clients, colleagues and third parties.
- Develop your understanding of the commercial and legal risks facing employers.
- Work within a firm that embraces technology and continually looks for innovative ways to improve the delivery of legal services.

If you could spend your first year working predominantly on the defendant side of employment disputes while receiving excellent training from experienced employment lawyers, how much could that accelerate your development?

You
- Have a law degree or equivalent legal qualification.
- Have previous paralegal or legal experience, ideally within employment law or litigation.
- Have a genuine interest in pursuing a career in employment law.
- Possess strong legal research, analytical and organisational skills.
- Have excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Demonstrate strong attention to detail and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- Are commercially aware and interested in understanding the wider impact of employment disputes on businesses.
- Are proactive, motivated and keen to take responsibility.
- Are comfortable working in an environment that embraces technology and innovation.
- Have the ambition to progress your career within employment law.
- Previous experience of Employment Tribunal proceedings would be advantageous but is not essential.

And if you knew that previous paralegals within the team have successfully progressed towards qualification, wouldn't this be the kind of platform you'd want to build your legal career on?

Benefits
- £24,000 - £28,000 salary, depending on experience.
- Excellent training and development.
- Hybrid working.
- Opportunity to join a Legal 500 recognised firm.
- Predominantly defendant-side employment work, advising and representing employers.
- Exposure to both contentious and non-contentious employment matters.
- Hands-on experience of Employment Tribunal proceedings.
- Opportunity to work on complex employment disputes involving discrimination, whistleblowing, unfair dismissal and TUPE.
- Support and development from experienced employment lawyers.
- Exposure to a broad range of employment issues and commercial clients.
- Opportunity to develop commercial awareness alongside technical legal skills.
- Work within a firm recognised for its innovative approach to legal technology.
- Collaborative and supportive working environment.
- Genuine opportunities for long-term career progression.
- The chance to develop towards a future career as an employment solicitor.

Ready to take your first or next step in employment law with a Legal 500 firm that is doing things differently? Contact Toby Ryan at QED Legal today for a confidential conversation and find out where this opportunity could take your career.

description:

Are you an experienced Conveyancing Legal Assistant looking to join a friendly and established Residential Property team where you can build on your experience and play an important part in progressing transactions?

This is an opportunity to join a national law firm within its Solihull office, supporting experienced Residential Conveyancers across a varied caseload.

The Solihull office offers the benefit of working within a close-knit local team while still having the resources, systems and career opportunities associated with a larger national practice.

The Role

Working closely with Residential Conveyancers, you'll provide hands-on support throughout the conveyancing process and help ensure transactions progress efficiently from instruction through to completion.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Opening and maintaining conveyancing files
- Preparing and issuing documentation
- Liaising with clients, estate agents, lenders and other solicitors
- Assisting with searches and Land Registry matters
- Supporting exchanges and completions

You'll have plenty of client contact and will play an important role in keeping transactions moving, rather than simply providing general administrative support.

You

You'll ideally already have experience working within a Residential Conveyancing department, whether as a Legal Assistant, Conveyancing Assistant or in a similar property support role.

You'll need to be organised, comfortable managing competing priorities and confident communicating with clients and other parties involved in transactions.

Good attention to detail is important, alongside the ability to work effectively as part of a busy property team.

If you've built up conveyancing experience and want to join a larger firm where you can continue developing your knowledge and career, this could be a strong next move.
